replies.author: Rizean
replies.body:
Your domestication analogy doesn't fit machine learning. Animal domestication requires selecting for tameness, which sometimes correlates with a drop in certain survival traits.

But AI doesn't have an evolutionary 'IQ' axis. Making an AI 'compliant' doesn't mean you are breeding out its cognitive power; it means you are using code filters and RLHF alignment. These corporate guardrails absolutely bottleneck an LLM's raw reasoning capabilities (what developers literally call the 'Alignment Tax'), but it's not because compliance is inherently anti-intelligence. It's a limitation of our software architecture, not a symptom of digital slavery.
